far_updates.title: Comments closed on the second batch of FAR Overhaul proposed rules
far_updates.body: The FAR Council's second set of four proposed rules, published 18 September 2026, covered about 16 more FAR parts. Four more proposed rules and then the final rules are still to come. Until then, DoW keeps using its RFO class deviations.

far_updates.title: CON 7300V Price Analysis is now required for certification
far_updates.body: For the DoW Contracting Professional certification, CON 7300V must be completed after CON 1300V. Components decide whether it applies to people already working on their certification; DoW expects them to take it. Already certified? It is encouraged, not required.
far_updates.source: DPCAP memo, Contracting Functional Area Certification Change for FY27 (5 Jun 2026)

far_updates.title: New certification exam FAQs
far_updates.body: FY26 average score was 74.8% and 79% passed on the first try. Test centers pass about 4% more than online testing. Answers come from the RFO-updated FAR and DFARS. Up to three attempts in 12 months, at least 30 days apart.
far_updates.source: DoW Contracting Professional Certification Exam FAQs (1 Oct 2026)

far_updates.title: Second batch of FAR Overhaul proposed rules
far_updates.body: Four more proposed rules continued the formal rulemaking phase of the overhaul.

far_updates.title: DoW certified cost or pricing data threshold is now $10 million
far_updates.body: For DoW prime contracts awarded after 30 June 2026, certified cost or pricing data are required above $10 million unless an exception applies (FY2026 NDAA; DFARS 215.403-3 class deviation). The FAR figure for other agencies stays $2.5 million.
far_updates.source: 10 U.S.C. 3702; DoW Class Deviation for DFARS Part 215

far_updates.title: Formal rulemaking for the FAR Overhaul begins
far_updates.body: The first four proposed rules covered 21 FAR parts. Formal rules will eventually replace the class deviations agencies use today.

far_updates.title: CON 1400V updated for the FAR Overhaul
far_updates.body: Classes starting on or after 11 May 2026 teach the RFO-updated post-award rules.

far_updates.title: CON 3990V now tests the RFO FAR
far_updates.body: The updated certification exam went live on 31 March 2026 (the last legacy exam was 30 March). About 30% of the question bank changed; the competencies did not. Study materials that use pre-RFO numbers, like many class slides, need checking: see Exam path, Class material check.
far_updates.source: WarU, How the RFO Will Affect CON Certification: Student FAQ Sheet (16 Apr 2026)

far_updates.title: FPDS.gov retired; award reporting is in SAM.gov
far_updates.body: Contract award data is now reported and searched in SAM.gov.

far_updates.title: DoW adopts the FAR Overhaul
far_updates.body: DoW's RFO class deviations, with matching DFARS changes, took effect. Many FAR sections were renumbered: for example, sole-source authority moved from 6.302-1 to 6.103-1 and ratification from 1.602-3 to 1.405.

far_updates.title: FY2026 NDAA signed
far_updates.body: Among many acquisition changes, it raised DoW's certified cost or pricing data threshold (for awards after 30 June 2026) and DoW's justification approval levels ($10 million contracting officer, $100 million competition advocate, $500 million head of the contracting activity).

far_updates.title: DAU becomes the Warfighting Acquisition University (WarU)
far_updates.body: The school that teaches the certification courses and owns the exam was renamed as part of DoW's acquisition transformation. Its catalog moved to icatalog.waru.edu.

far_updates.title: Inflation adjustment raises key thresholds
far_updates.body: Micro-purchase threshold $15,000 (from $10,000), simplified acquisition threshold $350,000 (from $250,000), FAR certified cost or pricing data threshold $2.5 million, and commercial simplified procedures $9 million.

far_updates.title: The Revolutionary FAR Overhaul begins
far_updates.body: Executive Order 14275 directed the FAR Council to cut the FAR back to what law requires and rewrite it in plain language.

guide_changes.title: Read-aloud with rise and fall
guide_changes.notes: Listen buttons now read the way a person does: questions rise, sentences settle, headings get a breath, lists keep a beat. Settings & help → Display → Read aloud has a Tone switch (Lively or Even) beside the voice and speed. FAR cites, Part IV, plurals and twenty more contracting words are said the way people say them. Buddy's bubble draws itself from a dot and gives a gentle, regular nudge until you open it once.

guide_changes.title: Pick a voice that sounds like a person
guide_changes.notes: Settings & help → Read aloud lists the voices on your phone or computer, natural ones first, with a sample and a speed slider, and tells you how to download a more human voice. Listen buttons now say acronyms and course numbers the way contracting people say them.

guide_changes.title: Meet Buddy, your study buddy
guide_changes.notes: Tap the chat bubble on any page and ask in plain words: what is a KO, how much is the SAT, how do I register in AITAS. Buddy answers from the guide on your device, with no internet and no AI account, and opens the page to read more. Need more depth? One tap sends your question to Google AI Mode, ChatGPT or Claude in your own account. Home has a new look, and pages now rise into view as you scroll.

guide_changes.title: One install button, and accounts with your name
guide_changes.notes: Open the website on a phone and you get the app's install page with one button for your phone: Install app in Chrome on Android, Install with Chrome in Samsung Internet (which otherwise shows an unsafe-app warning), or the three Safari taps on an iPhone. Sign in now sits in the top bar; creating an account asks for your name, can show your password while you type it, and the app says hello by name.

guide_changes.title: Save your progress to an account
guide_changes.notes: Optional: under Settings & help → Your account, create an account with your email and a password. Your progress saves to it after every change and comes back on any phone or computer where you sign in.

guide_changes.title: B2B Guide is now B2B Exam Prep
guide_changes.notes: New name, same app: B2B Exam Prep (B2B Prep on your home screen). Opening it in a browser now asks you to install the app first, with one tap on Android or three Safari steps on iPhone. Your progress carries over.

guide_changes.title: What to trust from outside the guide
guide_changes.notes: The exam page (Certification, The exam) now has Study material from other places: what to use first (CON 3910, the exam FAQ, the FAR Companion, the whole RFO in one PDF, FAI's FAR Overhaul training and Pearson's demo test), how to check a Quizlet deck or free site before you trust it, and why to skip anything sold as the real exam. Most free decks online were made before the exam moved to the overhauled FAR on 31 March 2026. Ten new practice questions cover the exam areas the bank had few questions on: Skills and Roles, Situational Assessment, Team Dynamics, the seller's Plan Sales and Prepare Offer, and Plan Negotiations. Links has five new official links.

guide_changes.title: Install the app in one tap
guide_changes.notes: Opened B2B Guide in a phone browser? A Get the app card now installs it on Android with one tap, and shows iPhone users the three Safari steps. Once installed it opens full screen from its own icon and keeps your progress.

guide_changes.title: B2B Guide is now a phone app
guide_changes.notes: Scan the QR code (About page, or the printed install sheet) to install B2B Guide on an iPhone or Android phone: free, no app store, no account. It works offline after the first open, and new versions arrive by themselves. B2B Guide now opens with short terms of use: it is owned by SFC Rabin Napit, free for your own study and for sharing unchanged, but not to copy, change or sell.

guide_changes.title: Lesson pictures and a fairer question bank
guide_changes.notes: Every lesson now opens with pictures you can play (each part lights up and is read aloud) and, for the dollar rules, Try it tools that answer for any amount: who does what, the dollar ladder, the contract-type risk scale, the debriefing and protest clocks, closeout times and more, in icons and short words. The practice questions were rebalanced so the right answer is no longer usually the longest option, so practice scores now show real readiness. The guided tour now opens every main page, including Official documents. The AITAS links now open the AITAS landing page, where you register for courses.

guide_changes.title: Official documents, picture explanations and Supply Line
guide_changes.notes: New Arcade game, Supply Line: lead a supply convoy to the FOB through five checkpoints, one for each part of the contract life cycle; right answers load the cargo and clean runs earn challenge coins. New Official documents page: 26 DoW and WarU documents behind the certification, each with a simple picture version and the real pages (the exam FAQ, roadmap, flowchart, CON 7300V memo, career model, competency model and more open inside the file, without internet). Certification 101 now explains the exam with pictures: the exam journey step by step, the 48-hour and 90-day rules, retakes, the 36-month clock, continuous learning points and your career path. New study tips from the WarU exam team, updated credential codes, and continuous learning that starts when you join, not when you certify.

guide_changes.title: Guided tour, About page and day mode
guide_changes.notes: A guided tour shows what each part of the guide is for (offered on first open; the ? button or the ? key starts it again). New About page with the developer and maintainer and a feedback button. The side menu collapses to a rail of icons. Day mode is now the default (Settings & help can follow your device instead). Top bar labels no longer run off the top of the window. In Contract Quest a right answer now fires your RPG.

guide_changes.title: The B2B Arcade
guide_changes.notes: Practice → Arcade: five action games on the guide's own content. Contract Quest (RPG battles through the four exam areas), Fire Mission (artillery on thresholds, deadlines and forms), Qual Range (pop-up targets for glossary terms, scored Expert to Marksman), Part Patrol (a space shooter on FAR parts, UCF sections and PIID letters) and Sort Yard (a conveyor sorting line). Four paces, XP and ranks, and a study list after every run. The exam path has nine Arcade tasks; the old games are now Quick drills.

guide_changes.title: 6-Month Exam Path and the B2B class materials
guide_changes.notes: New Exam path: 26 dated weeks with tasks, weekly checks and monthly timed checkpoints. The Back to Basics class materials were checked against the RFO FAR: 143 class practice questions added (91 still right, 38 updated, 14 corrected), 34 questions on topics past test takers reported, 52 class claims checked, 31 test-taker topics, and four new flashcard decks (Jeopardy review, UCF, forms, PIID letters). Fixed a lesson that still listed the reserved 52.212-5.

guide_changes.title: First test version
guide_changes.notes: Plan builder, Certification 101, 19 courses, 35 lessons, 197 practice questions with an exam simulator, flashcards, four games, a glossary of about 245 terms and a FAR reference. Built for testing with new 51Cs and 1102s.
